arms.description: Baseline: optid is not running at all. The machine keeps its power-on control values for the whole trajectory.
No-change control: the real daemon runs with every domain off. Any control value that moves here is a defect in the off path.
Fully enabled: every supported domain may actuate together, with the simulated hardware verified by an administrator allowlist override.
Fully enabled with the shipped seeded allowlist and no administrator override — the configuration a real installation starts in.
Every domain in observe mode: optid computes the same decisions and suppresses every write.
Deliberately harmful control: a policy whose mode table asks for the worst plausible values for the workload in force.
Isolation arm: only the cpu_epp domain may actuate; every other domain is off.
Isolation arm: only the platform_profile domain may actuate; every other domain is off.

assumptions.description: Mid-range 15 W-class mobile x86 laptop, flash storage, single internal panel. Central estimates.
EPP and platform profile barely move performance or power (firmware ignores most of the hint).
EPP and platform profile move performance and power strongly (aggressive firmware).
Deep idle is shallow-exit and barely cheaper than a shallow state, so a PM QoS floor costs almost no energy.
Deep idle saves a lot and exits slowly, so a PM QoS floor is a large energy cost and a large latency win.
Link power management saves little and costs little (ASPM/ALPM barely engage).
Link power management saves a lot and costs a lot of wake latency.
Small chassis: high thermal resistance, fast time constant, early throttle.
Large chassis: low thermal resistance, slow time constant, late throttle.
Bright, power-hungry panel dominates the platform power budget.
Swappiness barely changes reclaim behaviour; dirty limits barely change writeback.

notes: Crash recovery was exercised through the production daemon restart path (reconciler hydrate, journal replay and handback), after clearing the tmpfs state directory to simulate a reboot.

The standalone S3D `optid-recover` executable was run as a real subprocess before every supervised restart, matching `optid-apply.service`'s `Requires=optid-recover.service`. Its `--machine-root` flag, which exists only in a `test-simulation` build, rebases every recorded target path into the simulated machine, so no recovery write can reach a host path.

The `cgroup_reweight` domain is held off in every arm: actuating it means executing `systemctl` against real system services, which this harness must never do. It is reported as unsupported in simulation, not as a passing test.

scenarios.description: Screen on, nothing running, on battery. The classic case for depth.
Desktop use on AC: editing, browsing, moderate wakeups.
Latency-critical foreground work on AC with a high wakeup rate.
Sustained compile-style throughput on AC; the machine is CPU bound.
Working set larger than resident memory; reclaim is on the critical path.
Storage-bound work: high IOPS and heavy writeback.
Background work throughout, with a latency-critical foreground application arriving and leaving (the GameMode / foreground pin path).
Sustained load with an external heat source that drives the die into the throttle band, then is removed so the machine recovers.
The charger is unplugged mid-run and plugged back in.
Device and CPU hotplug under a running daemon; the capability topology changes twice.
policy.toml is replaced with unparseable content under the running daemon, then repaired.
A kernel control starts refusing writes, a second is truncated, and a third drifts under optid. The circuit breaker is expected to open.
faults: writes to /sys/firmware/acpi/platform_profile are refused from cycle 2
the write to /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu0/cpufreq/energy_performance_preference is truncated at cycle 3
a third party sets /proc/sys/vm/swappiness to 1 at cycle 4

scenarios.description: The daemon dies mid-run without restoring. A later start must find the journal and hand the machine back.
faults: the daemon dies without restoring after cycle 3

scenarios.description: Restoration itself fails at shutdown: the control refuses the handback write. The workload drives the platform profile away from its power-on value, so there is a real handback to refuse.
faults: restoration of /sys/firmware/acpi/platform_profile is refused at shutdown

scenarios.description: The die sensor disappears and a pressure file goes unparseable while the daemon is running.
